newsitem.title: INDIA: Doctors to fix Mother Teresa's heartbeat again.
newsitem.headline: Doctors to fix Mother Teresa's heartbeat again.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Monday that they planned a second attempt to correct the 86-year-old nun's irregular heartbeat after it began faltering again.

Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular update on the Roman Catholic missionary's condition that they had not yet set a date for repeating the procedure, which she underwent last Wednesday.
The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner had surgery last month to unblock two coronary arteries, her third such operation in five years.
Last Wednesday they gave the revered nun, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, a mild electric shock, called cardioversion, to correct her irregular heartbeat.

"Doctors feel that they should attempt cardioversion one more time and give her the benefit of sinus (regular) rhythm since they know this makes a tremendous difference in her with regard to short-term and long-term prognosis," the hospital said.
It said the recurrence of irregular heartbeat had not damaged Mother Teresa's heart, and she was talkative and had listened to morning mass.
